title: Kaiserschmarrn
subtitle: austrian torn pancake with stewed plums
excerpt: Kaiserschmarrn is a thick, fluffy Austrian baked pancake torn into irregular pieces and dusted with icing sugar, served alongside stewed plums. It is one of the most beloved desserts in Austrian and Bavarian cooking. Serves 4.
sourceNotes: The name means 'Emperor's mess', referencing Emperor Franz Joseph I of Austria who reportedly loved the dish. It has been served in Alpine huts and Viennese coffee houses for over a century.

glossaryTerms.definition: The stage where beaten egg whites hold firm, upright peaks when the whisk is lifted, adding lightness and lift to the pancake batter.
An Austrian word meaning a torn or scrambled dish. In cooking, it refers to a baked pancake that is torn into pieces in the pan rather than turned whole.

content.text: The lightness of kaiserschmarrn comes from folding beaten egg whites to
into the batter, then finishing in the oven. The
step, tearing the pancake into rough chunks, is what gives it its character. Serves 4.
Use a large ovenproof frying pan. The batter goes in the pan, into the oven, and is torn apart there before serving.
Make the stewed fruit first: combine the apple, sugar, and lemon juice in a medium saucepan with 3 tablespoons of water. Cook over medium heat for 10 to 15 minutes until tender. Set aside.
Preheat the oven to 180C. Whisk the egg yolks with 20g of the sugar, the cream, flour, and vanilla until smooth.
In a clean bowl, whisk the egg whites with the remaining 20g of sugar until they hold stiff peaks. Fold gently into the yolk batter in two additions, keeping as much air as possible.

Melt the butter in a large ovenproof frying pan over medium heat. Pour in the batter and cook for 2 minutes until the edges just begin to set. Transfer to the oven and bake for 10 to 12 minutes until puffed and golden.

Remove from the oven. Using two forks or a spatula, tear the pancake into irregular pieces directly in the pan. Dust generously with icing sugar. Serve immediately with the warm stewed fruit alongside.
The egg whites were not beaten to stiff peaks, or they were folded too vigorously. Be gentle when folding so the air stays in the batter.

attrs.problem: Pancake is still raw in the centre

content.text: Give it another 3 to 5 minutes in the oven. It should feel firm to the touch and golden on top before you tear it.
Dust the icing sugar on the torn pieces right at the moment of serving, not earlier. It will melt quickly on a hot pancake.

Kaiserschmarrn is eaten across Austria and Bavaria, often as a main course at lunchtime in mountain huts or as a dessert at home. It is one of the few dishes named after an Austrian emperor. The mess in the name is part of the point: torn, irregular, dusted with sugar, and eaten straight from the pan.
